title: How far is the meeting point of two circles from both centres?
description: Two circles of radius five centimetres are drawn with centres B and C, and they meet at the top point of the house. The video finds how far that point is from B and from C. Keeko's doubt is that only one distance is known, and the video breaks it.
teaching_notes: One idea: a point on a circle is at the radius from that circle's centre, so a point on two circles is at the radius from both centres. Watch for students who use only one circle.

source: The two circles of radius 5 cm centred at B and at C meet at
video_script.why: A learner sees that the point where two circles meet lies on both, so it is the radius away from both centres.
video_script.substitution: the book's two circles of radius five centimetres centred at B and at C, meeting at the top point A of the house
video_script.anchor: the book's house with the two circles of radius 5 cm centred at B and at C meeting at the top point A
video_script.wrong_answer: we cannot say how far it is from cee
video_script.wrong_move: uses only one of the two circles and leaves the other distance unknown
video_script.payoff_line: The point is five centimetres from bee and five centimetres from cee.

final_answer.value: 5 cm from B and 5 cm from C
final_answer.spoken: it is five centimetres away from both bee and cee

maths_rules: every point of a circle is at the radius distance from its centre
the point A lies on the circle centred at B with radius 5 cm, so AB = 5 cm
the point A also lies on the circle centred at C with radius 5 cm, so AC = 5 cm
a point on both circles is 5 cm from both centres
video_script.design: The house stays on the board with its two corners B and C. Two circles of radius five centimetres grow from B and C, and the point where they cross is marked A.

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about drawing a house.
<bookmark mark='circles'/>Two circles of radius five centimetres are drawn with centres bee and cee. They meet at the top point eigh.
How far is it from each centre?

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='radii'/>Every point of a circle is the same distance from its centre, and that distance is the radius.

beats.on_screen: Given: circles of radius 5 cm with centres B and C meet at a point A
narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, two circles of radius five centimetres with centres bee and cee. They meet at a point eigh.

beats.on_screen: To find: (a) the distance of A from B; (b) the distance of A from C

marks.find: the two questions are written under the given line

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find how far eigh is from bee, and how far it is from cee.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: A is on the circle centred at B, so AB = 5 cm

marks.onb: the circle centred at B glows and the line AB is marked 5 cm

narration: <bookmark mark='onb'/>Step one, eigh is on the circle with centre bee. Then eigh bee is five centimetres.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: A is also on the circle centred at C, so AC = 5 cm

marks.onc: the circle centred at C glows and the line AC is marked 5 cm

narration: <bookmark mark='onc'/>Step two, eigh is also on the circle with centre cee. Then eigh cee is five centimetres as well.

beats.on_screen: Answer: (a) 5 cm from B; (b) 5 cm from C

marks.res: the point A is joined to B and to C with two lines marked 5 cm

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The point is five centimetres from bee and five centimetres from cee.
<bookmark mark='res'/>This is the top point eigh of the house.

narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

marks.fix: the circle centred at C glows and passes through A
marks.keep: the bubble is struck out and the line AC is marked 5 cm

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the point is five centimetres from bee. Then we cannot say how far it is from cee.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But the point is on the second circle too.
<bookmark mark='keep'/>A point on both circles is five centimetres from both centres.
